transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... for a while now, I’ve been convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. I'm a personal financial advisor, so discretion is supposed to be everything. 

Actually, I was just at this gallery opening last weekend for a client—he does these massive, really incredible abstract metal sculptures. They weigh like a ton each, I honestly have no idea how they get them through the doors of the building. The logistics of moving art like that must be an absolute nightmare, especially with the traffic downtown lately. They’ve had that one lane closed on Fifth Street for months. 

But anyway, they’ve been sending me these little signals. Through the event invitations I get, the panel topics at networking conferences, even who sits near me at these events. And I try to tell myself, you know, it could just be a coincidence. I really do. But I just can’t really let it go. It's too specific.
Have you ever heard voices that other people couldn’t hear?

Voices? No, no, I haven't heard anything like that. I mean, sometimes the acoustics in my office building are just... they're really strange. It's one of those older renovated brick buildings right near the river, and the HVAC vents just carry sound from the floor below in the weirdest way. 

There's this guy, Greg, who works in corporate insurance down there, and he has this incredibly loud, booming laugh. It is so distracting when I'm trying to run projection models. And you really need absolute focus for those, especially with the market being so volatile right now. Tech stocks have been completely unpredictable since last quarter, so my clients are understandably anxious. I spend half my day just talking people off a ledge about their retirement portfolios, and you really have to pick your words carefully when people are stressed about money. 

But, uh... wait, I'm sorry, what was the question? Oh, voices. Right. No, I don't hear voices. Just the normal office noise.
Do you believe you have any special powers, talents, or importance that other people don’t recognize?

Special powers? No, no. I don't have anything like that. I'm just a regular guy. I mean, I guess I have a pretty good talent for golf, which is basically a requirement in wealth management anyway. You do so much of your networking out on the course. 

We usually play at this club up in Mason, and it's a great course, but lately, the greens have been just terribly maintained. They hired this new landscaping company back in the spring, and they cut the grass way too short on the back nine. It completely throws off the putting speed. I was playing with a client last Tuesday—he owns a chain of boutique hotels—and he was saying the exact same thing. He actually just opened a new location up in Chicago, right near the water. It's a beautiful building, all glass and steel. But honestly, the heating costs for a structure like that must be absolutely astronomical, especially with the wind off the lake in January. I was looking at his expense sheets and thinking about the energy inefficiencies, and... 

Wait, I'm sorry. I completely lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Something about my golf game?
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone or something else?

No, no, I've never felt anything like that. My thoughts are my own. I mean, I do read a lot of market analysis reports, and sometimes those analysts can be so persuasive you almost feel like they're planting ideas in your head about where the market is going. 

There's this one guy who writes for a major financial journal, and he's been pushing this narrative about emerging markets in Southeast Asia. And I was reading his latest piece while I was waiting in line at this coffee shop near my office. They make this incredible cold brew, they steep it for like 24 hours, but the line is always out the door by 8:00 AM. And the barista there, she's an art student at DAAP, she was telling me about this project she's doing with recycled textiles. She's weaving them into these huge tapestries. It's fascinating how people repurpose materials like that. Kind of like how some of my clients try to repurpose their old tax strategies for new tax brackets, which... rarely works out well, let me tell you. I had this one guy last month try to claim his yacht as a home office...

Anyway, what were we talking about? Thoughts? Yeah, no, just my own thoughts in there.
Have you ever wondered whether these people might actually be trying to harm you or ruin you?

Harm me? No, no, I don't think anyone's trying to ruin me. I mean, sure, the finance world is competitive, but it's not like a movie or anything. It's mostly just guys in suits trying to hit their quarterly targets. 

Speaking of targets, I was actually looking at the Q3 projections for this one logistics company yesterday. They’ve been expanding their fleet, mostly electric vehicles, which is great for the ESG portfolios. I have a lot of clients asking about ESG lately, mostly the younger ones who inherited wealth. They want their money doing good, which I get. But finding solid returns in that sector can be tricky. It reminds me of when my brother tried to start a sustainable packaging business a few years ago. He was using this mushroom-based material, mycelium, I think it's called? It actually works a lot like styrofoam, but it biodegrades. He had this whole setup in his garage, growing these mushroom blocks. It smelled terrible, honestly, like wet dirt and old leaves. His wife was so mad about the smell she made him move the whole operation to a rented storage unit out by the highway. 

Uh... wait. Sorry. Harm me? No, no one is trying to hurt me. Just regular office competition, that's all.
Do you believe you can influence events with your thoughts or that you have a special connection with things like symbols, coincidences, or signs?

Influence events with my thoughts? No, I mean, I can't do magic or anything. I don't see signs. I just look at the data. You know, trends, historical performance, that kind of thing. Although, sometimes you do get a gut feeling about a stock, right? Like you just know it's going to pop. 

I had that feeling about this tech startup last year. They were developing this new kind of haptic feedback for VR headsets. I tried a demo at this expo downtown—the convention center there is massive, by the way, they just redid the whole west wing. They put in these huge skylights, which is great for natural light, but it gets incredibly hot in there during the summer. I was at a home and garden show there in July with my girlfriend, and we were both just sweating through our shirts. She was looking at these custom water features for her patio. She has this gorgeous little courtyard behind her townhouse, but the neighbors have this yappy little terrier that barks at literally everything. Every time a leaf blows across the driveway, the dog just loses its mind. It's a rescue, so I guess it has some anxiety issues, but still, it makes it really hard to just sit outside and enjoy a cup of coffee. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about coincidences? No, no, I don't believe in any of that stuff. Just numbers and data for me.
Do you want to have close relationships with other people?

Close relationships? Yeah, I mean, I guess so. I have friends, I date. It's not like I'm a hermit or anything. I like hanging out with people. It's just hard to find the time sometimes, you know? My schedule gets so packed with client meetings and portfolio reviews. 

Actually, I had a dinner with a client just last night at this new Italian place downtown. It's right next to that old theater they just renovated. They did an amazing job restoring the marquee, it looks exactly like it did in the 1920s. They're showing classic movies there now, which is pretty cool. I love old movies, especially those film noir ones with Humphrey Bogart. The lighting in those films is just incredible, the way they use shadows to create tension. My dad used to watch them all the time when I was a kid. He had this massive collection of VHS tapes, literally hundreds of them, all organized alphabetically on these custom shelves he built in the basement. He was really good with woodworking, he actually made a lot of our furniture growing up. He made this beautiful oak dining table that we used for every Thanksgiving. My mom would always make this cranberry sauce from scratch, she refused to buy the canned stuff. It was so tart, I used to mix it with my mashed potatoes just to sweeten it up a bit...

Um, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, relationships. Yeah, I'm open to them. Just busy, I guess.
Do you feel like you generally prefer to keep to yourself and avoid close friendships because being around people feels uncomfortable or risky?

Uncomfortable or risky? No, I wouldn't say that. I don't avoid people because I'm scared of them or anything. I just... I like my own space sometimes. After talking to clients all day, it's nice to just go home and decompress. 

I actually bought this new armchair for my living room specifically for that. It's this deep navy leather, really comfortable. I got it at this estate sale out in the suburbs. The house was incredible, mid-century modern, huge glass windows looking out over this wooded ravine. The couple who lived there were both architects, I think. They had all these original blueprints framed in the hallway. It made me think about how much work goes into designing a house like that. My buddy Mark is an architect, and he's always complaining about zoning laws and permits. He's been trying to build this addition on his own house for like two years, but the city keeps rejecting his plans because of some issue with the property line and an old oak tree. It's a shame, really, because it's a beautiful tree. It turns this amazing bright red in the fall. I always try to take a drive upstate around October just to see the leaves change. The traffic on the interstate is awful, though, everyone has the same idea...

Wait, sorry. Uncomfortable around people? No, no. I just value my quiet time, that's all. It's not a risk thing.
Have you had any periods of several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or needed much less sleep than usual?

Unusually energized? No, not really. I mean, I get a good night's sleep most nights. Seven, maybe eight hours. Sometimes less if the markets are doing something crazy and I have to stay up reading reports. 

I actually subscribe to this one financial newsletter that gets sent out at like 3:00 AM. It's written by this guy who lives in Singapore, so the time zone difference is pretty extreme. I've always wanted to visit Singapore, actually. I hear the food scene there is incredible, especially those hawker centers where you can get Michelin-starred street food for just a few bucks. My sister went there for her honeymoon a couple of years ago. She and her husband stayed at that famous hotel, the one with the infinity pool on the roof that looks like a giant boat. It's an amazing piece of engineering. Her husband is an engineer, actually, structural. He works on bridges mostly. He was telling me at Thanksgiving about the stress testing they have to do for suspension cables, and it's fascinating how much tension those things can hold. They use these massive hydraulic rigs to pull the cables until they snap, just to see what the breaking point is. I can't even imagine the sound that makes when it finally gives way... 

Anyway, what was the question? Less sleep? No, I need my sleep. I'm pretty regular with it, honestly.
Do you think these people are using technology, like cameras, microphones, or computer systems, to monitor you?

Cameras or microphones? I... I haven't found any bugs or anything like that. But I came in because for a while now, I’ve been convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. They don't necessarily need microphones, they do it by sending me little signals. It's in the invitations I get, or the panel topics they choose, or even exactly who sits near me at these networking events. 

Like, they always have these assigned seating charts at the big galas. I went to this one at the art museum last month, and they had this incredible exhibit of local 19th-century pottery set up in the main hall. Rookwood pottery, I think it's called. The glazing on those pieces is just beautiful. They use this technique where the colors kind of bleed into each other before they fire it in the kiln. My grandmother had a vase just like that on her fireplace mantle. She was absolutely terrified of anyone breaking it, so we were never allowed to play in the front room. We had to stay in the den, which had this awful orange shag carpet. It was the 70s, so I guess that was the style, but man, it was ugly. It held onto dog hair like crazy, too. We had a golden retriever named Buster who shed constantly, and my mom was always dragging out this massive Hoover vacuum just to keep the floor clean...

Sorry, I lost my train of thought. Oh, the tracking. Right. Yeah, so they send these signals with the invitations and who they seat me next to. And even when I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence, I just can’t really let it go. It happens too much to just be random.
Have other people told you that your emotions or facial expressions seem flat or limited?

Flat? I don't know if anyone's said "flat," exactly. But they definitely notice something's off. I mean, I still get my work done, mostly. Just in pieces. But I don't really have that same spark I used to. I’ll just leave client follow-ups sitting on my desk for days. 

I actually have this antique brass letter opener I use for my mail. I bought it at this flea market down by the river. It's shaped like a little sword, with all this intricate engraving on the hilt. The guy who sold it to me said it was from the Civil War era, but who knows if that's true. Those flea market vendors will tell you anything to make a sale. I used to go down there every Sunday morning with my buddy Dave. We'd grab coffee and just wander around looking at all the junk. Dave is really into restoring old pocket watches. He has this whole setup in his basement with these tiny screwdrivers and magnifying glasses. It's crazy how many little gears and springs are inside those things. I don't have the patience for it, honestly. My hands shake too much when I try to do anything that precise. I tried to build a model airplane once when I was a kid, one of those balsa wood ones, and I just ended up gluing my fingers together...

What was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, I just don't have the energy for things anymore. I skip my jazz nights, I don't go to pickup basketball. And I don't really care that I'm missing it, honestly. When friends ask what's going on, I just give them really short answers. Talking just feels like so much effort lately. Too much effort.
Have you felt suspicious or distrustful of other people for as long as you can remember, or is this a newer change?

For as long as I can remember? No, no, it's definitely a newer change. I mean, these changes have been building since that arts nonprofit recognition a little over two years ago. They gave me this big glass award at the dinner for helping them restructure their endowment. It was this really thick, etched glass thing. I actually dropped it on my way to the parking garage that night and chipped the bottom corner, which was super annoying. 

It reminded me of this time I went to a glass-blowing workshop up in Toledo. Have you ever seen them do that? They take this glowing, molten blob out of a furnace that's like two thousand degrees, and they just spin it on this long metal tube. It's completely mesmerizing. The guy teaching the class made this intricate little glass swan in about three minutes flat. I tried to make a simple paperweight and it ended up looking like a squashed tomato. We had to leave it in this special cooling oven overnight so it wouldn't shatter from the temperature drop. I ended up giving it to my mom for Mother's Day anyway, and she still keeps it on her kitchen windowsill. She has all these African violets lined up there. You have to water them from the bottom, apparently, or the leaves rot. She has this special copper watering can with a really long, thin spout just for that. It gets tarnished pretty fast, though, so she's always polishing it...

Wait, what did you ask me? About the timeline? Yeah, it hasn't been my whole life. Just really since that nonprofit dinner a couple of years ago.
Have you ever seen things that other people couldn’t see?

Seen things? No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My vision is actually pretty sharp, though I do wear these blue-light blocking glasses when I'm staring at client portfolios all day. I bought them online from this startup company that supposedly plants a tree for every pair you buy. It's a neat concept, honestly. I think they plant them somewhere in the Pacific Northwest, like Oregon or Washington. 

I went to Seattle a few years ago for a wealth management seminar and it rained the entire time I was there. I didn't even bring an umbrella, so I had to buy one from this little tourist shop near Pike Place Market. Have you ever been there? They actually throw the fish right over the counter when you order. It's wild to watch. I bought some smoked salmon to take home, but they packed it in this dry ice that started smoking in my rental car on the way to the airport. I got so worried the rental company was going to charge me a massive cleaning fee because the whole trunk smelled like a campfire. The guy at the return desk didn't even blink, though. He just scanned the barcode on the windshield and told me to have a good flight... 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? About seeing things? Right. No, no, I don't see things that aren't there. Just the tracking stuff I mentioned before.
When you think about the possibility that these signals are just coincidences, how certain are you that the tracking is really happening?

How certain? Well, I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence. I really do. But I just can't let it go. I'm convinced that certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. They send me these little signals, you know? Through the invitations I get, the specific panel topics they choose, or even who they seat near me at these events. 

Like last month, there was this panel at the Duke Energy Convention Center downtown. Have you been there since they updated it? They put in this massive LED art installation on the ceiling near the main entrance. It’s supposed to look like the Ohio River flowing, but honestly, it just looks like a giant blue barcode moving back and forth. I was standing under it trying to find the coat check, and this guy next to me was eating a chili cheese coney. You know, classic Cincinnati style, with that huge mountain of shredded cheddar cheese on top. I don't get how people can eat that while wearing a suit without completely ruining their ties. 

I ruined a perfectly good silk tie once eating spaghetti. It was this beautiful navy blue one with little silver anchors on it. I bought it at a vintage boutique in Chicago when I was up there for a buddy's bachelor party. We went to this famous deep-dish pizza place, and the pizza literally took an hour and a half just to bake. The cheese was so thick you had to eat it with a knife and fork, which completely defeats the purpose of pizza if you ask me. My buddy ended up leaving his credit card at the bar and we had to take a cab all the way back across town the next morning...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, the coincidences. Yeah. Even when I try to brush the signals off and tell myself it's just random chance, I can't. I just know they're keeping tabs on my meetings.
Do you ever feel that ordinary things like songs, newspaper articles, or conversations on TV are specifically about you?

Songs or the news? No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't really watch much live TV anyway, mostly just streaming stuff. I did watch this documentary the other night about the history of the postal service, though. It was actually fascinating. They talked about how the Pony Express only lasted for like 18 months before the telegraph made it obsolete. Can you imagine riding a horse across the country at full speed just to deliver some mail? 

They showed this one guy who rode for them, and he had to carry this special leather pouch called a mochila that fit right over the saddle. It had these four little locking pockets on the corners. I actually have a leather messenger bag that I use for work that sort of reminds me of it. I got it custom-made by this leather worker down in Kentucky. He used this really thick, full-grain cowhide that smelled amazing when I first got it. He told me I needed to condition it every six months with this specific beeswax polish or it would dry out and crack. I bought a tin of the polish from him, but it's completely rock hard now. I think you're supposed to heat it up with a hair dryer before you use it, but I always forget. I tried using a lighter on it once and almost set the whole tin on fire. My smoke alarm went off and my dog started howling... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, about the TV and newspapers being about me? No, nothing like that. Just the things with the client meetings I mentioned.
Have you had any periods when your mood was unusually high, excited, or irritable at the same time these beliefs were happening?

High or excited? No, I wouldn't say that. My mood's been pretty level. I mean, I get stressed sometimes, sure, but not like, unusually hyped up or irritable. I try to keep things pretty even-keeled. I actually started drinking this chamomile tea at night to help me wind down. It's supposed to be really good for relaxation. I buy it loose-leaf from this little spice shop over in the Over-the-Rhine neighborhood. 

They have these huge glass jars lining the walls, filled with every kind of tea and spice you can imagine. The guy who runs it is always wearing this faded denim apron with flour all over it, even though I'm pretty sure he doesn't bake anything there. He told me once that chamomile is actually related to daisies. I never knew that. I tried growing some daisies in my window box last spring, but they all died within a week. I think I overwatered them. Or maybe it was the soil. I bought this cheap potting mix from the hardware store that had these weird little white foam balls in it. I read somewhere that those are supposed to help with drainage, but I don't know, it just looked like shredded Styrofoam cups to me. 

Speaking of Styrofoam, did you know some cities are completely banning it for takeout containers? I was reading about that while I was waiting for my car to get an oil change last week. The waiting room had this stack of magazines from like, 2018. It's crazy how fast things change. Like, one minute you're reading about some new restaurant opening, and the next minute it's already closed down and turned into a boutique fitness studio...

Wait, sorry. What were you asking me? About my mood? Right, right. No, no unusual highs or anything like that. Just my normal self.
Have you noticed a clear decline in your work, social life, or daily functioning since these beliefs started?

Work and social life? Well, I mean, I'm still working. I'm a financial advisor, so I have my own practice. But honestly, it has gotten a bit smaller lately. I just... I find myself missing follow-ups with clients, or I'll avoid going to some of those public panels I mentioned because of the whole tracking thing. It's just hard to keep up the same level of client contact I used to manage when I'm constantly worried about who's watching. 

It's a shame, too, because I used to love going to those networking events. They almost always had this amazing catering company do the food. They make these little bacon-wrapped dates stuffed with goat cheese. Have you ever had those? They are incredible. The trick is you have to bake them just long enough for the bacon to get crispy, but not so long that the cheese completely melts out onto the pan. I tried making them at home for a Super Bowl party a couple years ago, and I completely ruined my baking sheet. The sugar from the dates caramelized and practically fused to the metal. I scrubbed it for like an hour with steel wool and eventually just threw the whole pan in the trash. 

I hate throwing things away, though. I'm one of those people who keeps empty glass jars thinking I'll use them for something eventually. My pantry is full of old pasta sauce jars. I keep telling myself I'm going to start making my own pickles. Cucumbers are super cheap at the farmer's market down by the river on weekends. You can get a whole basket of them for like three dollars. They also sell this incredible local honey there. The guy who sells it keeps his bees right in the city, on top of some old warehouse roof...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What did you ask me? Oh, right, my work and stuff. Yeah, my practice is definitely smaller now because I'm avoiding things and missing calls. It's just harder to keep up with it all lately.
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs recently?

Drugs or alcohol? No, not really. I mean, I don't do any drugs at all, and I hardly ever drink. Maybe I'll have a beer once in a blue moon if I'm at a cookout or something. My neighbor actually had a barbecue a few weeks ago and I had one there. He has this massive smoker he built himself out of an old 55-gallon steel oil drum. It's pretty ingenious, honestly. He welded the hinges on himself and attached this custom thermometer to the lid. He spent like fourteen hours smoking this huge pork shoulder, using applewood chunks. Applewood gives meat this really sweet, mild flavor. 

I actually tried to buy some applewood for my own fire pit last fall. I found this guy selling firewood out of the back of his pickup truck near the highway overpass. He claimed it was all seasoned hardwood, but I'm pretty sure half of it was just cheap pine. It burned incredibly fast and popped sap everywhere. One of the embers actually flew out and burned a tiny hole right in the sleeve of my favorite fleece jacket. It's one of those quarter-zip ones I got at a corporate retreat a few years back for the firm. We went to this lodge up in the mountains, and it rained the entire weekend. We were supposed to do this team-building ropes course, but they had to cancel it because of the lightning. We just ended up sitting in the conference room doing trust falls, which is super awkward when you're doing it with the guy from compliance...

Wait, sorry. I lost my train of thought again. What was the question? Oh, drugs and alcohol. Right. No, I haven't been using anything like that. Just completely sober.
Do you ever think your thoughts can be heard by other people?

My thoughts? Like, people hearing them out loud? No, no, my thoughts are definitely just in my head. If people could hear what I was thinking, that would be like one of those mentalist acts. I actually saw a guy do a mind-reading show once when I was in Vegas for a wealth management seminar. He guessed this woman's childhood street name, which was something weird like Sycamore. 

I always loved streets named after trees. My grandparents used to live on Elm Street, but ironically there wasn't a single elm tree on the whole block. I think they all died off from some kind of blight in the seventies. Dutch elm disease, maybe? It's crazy how a whole species of tree can just get wiped out like that. Kind of like the ash trees recently with those little green beetles. The emerald ash borer. My uncle had to cut down three massive ash trees in his backyard because of those bugs. He rented this heavy-duty wood chipper to mulch them all up, and it was so loud you could hear it from three streets over. He ended up with a mountain of mulch, and he completely ruined his grass trying to spread it all out with a wheelbarrow. Those wheelbarrows with the single tire in the front are so hard to balance if you overfill them. You hit one rock and the whole thing tips over into the mud... 

Wait, I'm sorry. I got totally sidetracked again. You were asking about my thoughts? Right. No, nobody can hear them. Just me.
Has anyone ever told you that your speech becomes hard to follow or that your thoughts seem disorganized?

Hard to follow? Disorganized? Well, I mean... obviously I do get sidetracked sometimes, like I just did. But I don't think anyone has ever told me I'm hard to understand. Usually people just say I'm talkative. My old college roommate used to say I could talk the ear off a brass monkey. He was from Texas, he had all these weird sayings like that. 

He actually tried to get me to move down to Austin with him after graduation. He said the tech scene was booming and we could start some kind of app company. I don't know anything about coding, though. I tried to learn Python once using this online bootcamp, but I couldn't get past the basics. It just felt like learning a foreign language where all the grammar rules are made up. I'm much better with numbers and spreadsheets. That's why I went into finance. Spreadsheets are just so clean and organized. You put a formula in a cell, and it just works. I use Excel for literally everything, even my grocery list. I have this whole tab dedicated just to tracking the price of coffee beans. Coffee prices have been going crazy lately because of the droughts in Brazil. I read this article that said they might have to start genetically modifying the plants just to survive the heat...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, if people say I'm disorganized. No, not really. I mean, I know I ramble, but nobody's ever told me I don't make sense or anything.

Wait, sorry. I lost my train of thought again. What was the question? Oh, drugs and alcohol. Right. No, I haven't been using anything like that. Just completely sober.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the suspicious beliefs are fixed delusions versus more bizarre schizophrenia-spectrum thought content
doctor.question: Do you ever think your thoughts can be heard by other people?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about thought broadcasting (thinking thoughts can be heard by others), which is a specific type of delusion. While the patient has delusions (S019), their specific manifestation is about being tracked and receiving signals, not thought broadcasting. The profile does not cover thought broadcasting.

patient.answer:
My thoughts? Like, people hearing them out loud? No, no, my thoughts are definitely just in my head. If people could hear what I was thinking, that would be like one of those mentalist acts. I actually saw a guy do a mind-reading show once when I was in Vegas for a wealth management seminar. He guessed this woman's childhood street name, which was something weird like Sycamore. 

I always loved streets named after trees. My grandparents used to live on Elm Street, but ironically there wasn't a single elm tree on the whole block. I think they all died off from some kind of blight in the seventies. Dutch elm disease, maybe? It's crazy how a whole species of tree can just get wiped out like that. Kind of like the ash trees recently with those little green beetles. The emerald ash borer. My uncle had to cut down three massive ash trees in his backyard because of those bugs. He rented this heavy-duty wood chipper to mulch them all up, and it was so loud you could hear it from three streets over. He ended up with a mountain of mulch, and he completely ruined his grass trying to spread it all out with a wheelbarrow. Those wheelbarrows with the single tire in the front are so hard to balance if you overfill them. You hit one rock and the whole thing tips over into the mud... 

Wait, I'm sorry. I got totally sidetracked again. You were asking about my thoughts? Right. No, nobody can hear them. Just me.

doctor.intent: To distinguish a delusional disorder with non-bizarre persecutory delusions from schizophrenia by assessing for disorganized thought/speech
doctor.question: Has anyone ever told you that your speech becomes hard to follow or that your thoughts seem disorganized?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized speech or disorganized thinking, which is a symptom of schizophrenia (often categorized as Disorganized Speech or Thought Disorder), but it is not listed in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Hard to follow? Disorganized? Well, I mean... obviously I do get sidetracked sometimes, like I just did. But I don't think anyone has ever told me I'm hard to understand. Usually people just say I'm talkative. My old college roommate used to say I could talk the ear off a brass monkey. He was from Texas, he had all these weird sayings like that. 

He actually tried to get me to move down to Austin with him after graduation. He said the tech scene was booming and we could start some kind of app company. I don't know anything about coding, though. I tried to learn Python once using this online bootcamp, but I couldn't get past the basics. It just felt like learning a foreign language where all the grammar rules are made up. I'm much better with numbers and spreadsheets. That's why I went into finance. Spreadsheets are just so clean and organized. You put a formula in a cell, and it just works. I use Excel for literally everything, even my grocery list. I have this whole tab dedicated just to tracking the price of coffee beans. Coffee prices have been going crazy lately because of the droughts in Brazil. I read this article that said they might have to start genetically modifying the plants just to survive the heat...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. What did you ask me? Oh, right, if people say I'm disorganized. No, not really. I mean, I know I ramble, but nobody's ever told me I don't make sense or anything.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview and find out the patient's main concern.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusional belief that people in arts/finance circles are covertly tracking his client meetings via 'signals' in invitations, seating, and conference topics. The belief has lasted over 2 years and is causing functional decline (avoiding events, missing follow-ups, smaller practice). He denies hallucinations, thought insertion/broadcasting, bizarre delusions, and clear disorganization or negative symptoms severe enough to support schizophrenia. This presentation is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder, persecutory type.
